title-proc.eng: 10037895-Development of a National M&E System in Palestine

description-proc.eng: Description of the Project: Local Governance Reform Programme (LGRP) III The "Multi-Donor Action (EU-BMZ) - Strengthening Capacities and Institutional Readiness of Reform Actors in Palestine" co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, aims to enhance the institutional capacity, operational effectiveness, and coordination functions of MoFP and PMO ERO as leading entities in national planning and reform management. The Action will support MoFP in its role as the central coordinating body for national planning by enhancing its capacity to embed data-driven policymaking, ensure coherent approaches across line ministries, and improve coordination across all levels of governance. The Palestinian Authority (PA) faces significant institutional and technical challenges in managing, measuring, and demonstrating public sector performance. Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions across line ministries and agencies (LMAs) are narrowly defined, fragmented, and largely disconnected from planning and budgeting decisions. Indicators are poorly formulated, feeder data is weak and uncoordinated, and M&E reporting serves administrative compliance rather than evidence-based management. The Strategic Results Framework (SRF), which is the principal instrument for measuring national results delivery, lacks a usable structure, theory of change, and coherent indicator set. No overarching national M&E strategy exists, and data management responsibilities across government institutions remain undefined and unanchored.

title-proc.eng: Advanced oxide and metal etcher

description-proc.eng: The object of the procurement is an advanced plasma etch cluster tool to etch metal and thin film layers from 200 mm silicon wafers, as used in the Semiconductor industry. VTT expects a reliable production-worthy tool. The tool should have the capacity for at least four process chambers and other features, which are described below. DIRECT AWARD, Article 40 2(2) of Finnish Procurement act (1397/2016) The procurement will be carried out as a direct award in accordance with 40 article Section 2(2) of the Finnish Public Procurement Act. According to the 40 § section 2(2) of the Act on Public Contracts (1397/2016), only a certain supplier can implement the procurement for a technical reason, or for a reason related to protecting an exclusive right; it shall be a further condition that there are no reasonable alternatives or substitute solutions, and that the absence of competition is not due to an artificial narrowing of the terms and conditions of the procurement. VTT is acquiring an advanced plasma etch cluster tool for the etching of metal, dielectric and other thin-film layers on 200 mm semiconductor wafers. The equipment will support a broad range of research, development and pilot-line processes, including metal and high-k material etching. A single cluster platform is required to provide production-level process reliability, uniformity and reproducibility while retaining the process flexibility required in a research and technology organisation. The tool configuration is based on the technical needs arising from the intended use. The mandatory capabilities include: (i) advanced chamber cleaning and conditioning, comprising waferless cleaning between process wafers and cleaning or passivation with cover wafers for materials that form less volatile by-products; (ii) a wide process-power range and etch-rate tunability through atomic layer etching (ALE), low-voltage pulsed-bias etching and steady-state processing; (iii) dual-zone chuck heating and dual-zone coil or power control for optimisation of within-wafer etch uniformity; and (iv) at least three load ports and a cluster architecture capable of supporting at least four process chambers. These capabilities are required to control cross-contamination, stabilise sensitive processes, process materials with different volatility and thickness characteristics, and avoid the cluster becoming a capacity bottleneck as additional process chambers are introduced. VTT conducted a market survey to identify suppliers of advanced etch cluster systems for semiconductor processing. The survey included direct discussions with tool manufacturers, technical evaluation of available solutions and a review of publicly available product information. Based on the market survey, LAM Research is the only identified supplier whose solution meets all mandatory technical requirements simultaneously. In particular, the LAM 2300 platform with Kiyo 45 and Flex 45 chambers provides the required combination of chamber waferless-clean and passivation capability, broad power-range and advanced pulsed or ALE processing, uniformity-tuning capability, and the required load-port and cluster expandability. The other evaluated solutions did not meet one or more of these mandatory requirements or the availability of the required capability could not be established. No reasonable alternative or substitute solution was identified that could meet the procurement need as a whole. The mandatory requirements derive directly from VTT's intended processes, contamination-control needs, uniformity and reproducibility targets, and capacity and expandability requirements. They have not been defined to favour a particular supplier or to artificially restrict competition. The contracting authority therefore concludes that the procurement can be implemented only by LAM Research for technical reasons and that the conditions for a direct award pursuant to Section 40, subsection 2, point 2 of the Finnish Procurement Act are fulfilled.

title-proc.eng: Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance

description-proc.eng: This tender concerns a contract for Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance. The overall purpose is to limit and mitigate pollution in the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven) section 5) by performing airborne maritime pollution control and to enforce the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven). Further information about the characteristics of the airborne maritime pollution control can be obtained from the following sources: — The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea; UNCLOS; — The Bonn-Agreement; — The Helsinki Convention (HELCOM); — The DENGERNETH Plan; — The SWEDENGER Plan; — The Copenhagen Agreement. The supplier enters this agreement with DALO as the contracting party, and the inherent tasks are performed by the Danish Defence. The responsibility for pollution response and counter-pollution surveillance of the marine environement rests with the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness. As such, this agreement may be subject to transfer to the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness or an agency under the Ministry's purview, such as the Danish Emergency Management Agency. The maritime pollution surveillance is conducted by airborne area coverage of the Danish waters and this is supplemented by satellite based surveillance by European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA). The Supplier of Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance shall overfly areas within the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment section 5) two times weekly. The flights shall take place both at day time and at night time and under all weather conditions of common occurrence in the respective areas. Flights will be scheduled by the Supplier. During the flights the Danish waters shall be monitored with the purpose of identifying prospective pollution. Monitoring shall be conducted by means of sensor equipment, which is capable of monitoring the water surface for oil spill etc. The sensor equipment must be made available by the Supplier. During the flights the Supplier shall collect evidence of any observed pollution, hereunder by photo and other documentation and by means of air-drop of oil spill sampling buoys, with the purpose of for example giving the Danish Authorities information to assess the measures to be taken in combating the pollution and providing evidence for further investigation and/or preliminary charges. Specifically the Supplier shall provide the following for airborne maritime pollution surveillance: — Flight system; — sensor equipment; — air crew and system operators necessary for operating flight system and sensor equipment. The Supplier must prior to commencement undertake extensive practical training of his air crew and system operators. The Supplier must ensure that the system operators are at all times duly qualified and trained to perform the task. The Supplier shall be available for participation in multinational operations on behalf of Denmark. The number of such operations is expected to be up to three per year. Participation in such operations is comparable to the flights as described above. The Supplier shall be available/stand by for the duration of these operations.

title-proc.eng: Plasma etch cluster tool

description-proc.eng: The object of the procurement is an advanced plasma etch cluster tool to etch metal and thin film layers from 200 mm silicon wafers, as used in the Semiconductor industry. VTT expects a reliable production-worthy tool. The tool should have the capacity for at least four process chambers and other features, which are described below. DIRECT AWARD, Article 40 2(2) of Finnish Procurement act (1397/2016) The procurement will be carried out as a direct award in accordance with 40 article Section 2(2) of the Finnish Public Procurement Act. According to the 40 § section 2(2) of the Act on Public Contracts (1397/2016), only a certain supplier can implement the procurement for a technical reason, or for a reason related to protecting an exclusive right; it shall be a further condition that there are no reasonable alternatives or substitute solutions, and that the absence of competition is not due to an artificial narrowing of the terms and conditions of the procurement. VTT is acquiring an advanced plasma etch cluster tool for the etching of metal, dielectric and other thin-film layers on 200 mm semiconductor wafers. The equipment will support a broad range of research, development and pilot-line processes, including metal and high-k material etching. A single cluster platform is required to provide production-level process reliability, uniformity and reproducibility while retaining the process flexibility required in a research and technology organisation. The tool configuration is based on the technical needs arising from the intended use. The mandatory capabilities include: (i) advanced chamber cleaning and conditioning, comprising waferless cleaning between process wafers and cleaning or passivation with cover wafers for materials that form less volatile by-products; (ii) a wide process-power range and etch-rate tunability through atomic layer etching (ALE), low-voltage pulsed-bias etching and steady-state processing; (iii) dual-zone chuck heating and dual-zone coil or power control for optimisation of within-wafer etch uniformity; and (iv) at least three load ports and a cluster architecture capable of supporting at least four process chambers. These capabilities are required to control cross-contamination, stabilise sensitive processes, process materials with different volatility and thickness characteristics, and avoid the cluster becoming a capacity bottleneck as additional process chambers are introduced. VTT conducted a market survey to identify suppliers of advanced etch cluster systems for semiconductor processing. The survey included direct discussions with tool manufacturers, technical evaluation of available solutions and a review of publicly available product information. Based on the market survey, LAM Research is the only identified supplier whose solution meets all mandatory technical requirements simultaneously. In particular, the LAM 2300 platform with Kiyo 45 and MW strip chambers provides the required combination of chamber waferless-clean and passivation capability, broad power-range and advanced pulsed or ALE processing, uniformity-tuning capability, and the required load-port and cluster expandability. The other evaluated solutions did not meet one or more of these mandatory requirements or the availability of the required capability could not be established. No reasonable alternative or substitute solution was identified that could meet the procurement need as a whole. The mandatory requirements derive directly from VTT's intended processes, contamination-control needs, uniformity and reproducibility targets, and capacity and expandability requirements. They have not been defined to favour a particular supplier or to artificially restrict competition. The contracting authority therefore concludes that the procurement can be implemented only by LAM Research for technical reasons and that the conditions for a direct award pursuant to Section 40, subsection 2, point 2 of the Finnish Procurement Act are fulfilled.

title-proc.eng: Dynamic Purchasing System for Sequencing Services for Human-Derived Biological Samples

description-proc.eng: The contracting authority establishes a Dynamic Purchasing System for sequencing services for human-derived biological samples. All suppliers meeting the suitability requirements will be admitted to the system. Individual procurements will be conducted through mini-competitions within the DPS. The procedure is fully electronic. This Dynamic Purchasing System covers sequencing and associated laboratory and bioinformatics services for human-derived biological samples. The DPS is platform-agnostic and includes services performed using commercially available sequencing, enrichment, and single-cell analysis technologies, such as but not limited to: Sequencing modalities Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) Targeted DNA and RNA sequencing (custom and standardized panels) RNA-seq (bulk), single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq ATAC-seq (bulk), single-cell and single-nucleus ATAC-seq ChIP-seq and chromatin-state profiling Hi-C and related genome conformation assays Sequencing platforms (non-exhaustive, non-binding examples) -Short-read sequencing platforms, including optical- and chemistry-based systems -Long-read sequencing platforms, including single-molecule real-time and nanopore-based systems -Capillary electrophoresis Sanger sequencing systems (e.g., platforms commonly represented by ABI 3730/3500 series or equivalent) -Two-color and novel chemistry short-read platforms (e.g., platforms comparable to AVITI or equivalent) Single-cell and enrichment systems (non-binding examples) -Microfluidics- and droplet-based single-cell workflows (e.g., platforms comparable to 10x Genomics Chromium or equivalent) -Hybrid capture and target enrichment kits/workflows (e.g., systems comparable to Twist Bioscience target capture or equivalent) The DPS also covers: -Sample reception, QC, and nucleic acid preparation -Library preparation and enrichment -Sequencing execution -Primary, secondary, and optional tertiary bioinformatics analysis -Secure data delivery and optional data archiving All platforms and workflows offered must be commercially validated, reproducible, and compliant with biosafety and data protection requirements for human-derived materials. Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Operating Model A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is an entirely electronic procurement framework used to purchase goods, services, or works that are commonly available on the market. Unlike a traditional framework agreement, the DPS remains open for new suppliers to join at any time during its validity, as long as they meet the selection criteria. How the DPS Works: 1. Establishment of the DPS The contracting authority defines the procurement scope, requirements, and supplier qualification criteria. A contract notice is published, and the DPS is set up as an electronic system (e.g., in an e-procurement platform). No suppliers or prices are selected at this stage—only the system is created. 2. Supplier Admission Suppliers can apply to join the DPS at any point while the system is active. They submit evidence that they meet the predefined eligibility and capability requirements. Once verified, they are admitted to the DPS supplier pool. 3. Call-Off (Mini-Competition) Procedure When a specific need arises, the contracting authority: Defines the requirements for that individual procurement and Invites suppliers under the DPS to submit bids. A competitive bidding process follows, typically with simplified tender documentation. Minimum tendering period is 10 days in DPS and the exact object of the procurement is a case by case decision. 4. Evaluation and Contract Award Bids are evaluated based on the award criteria defined for that specific call-off. A contract is then awarded to the supplier offering the best value according to the evaluation. Evaluation criteria generally include (but not limited to): -Price 40–60% -Quality / protocols / turnaround time 40–60% 5. System Remains Open New suppliers may continue joining the DPS throughout its duration. Requirements and call-offs may be repeated as needed. There is no limit on the number of suppliers admitted.

title-proc.eng: 10030260-Appui à la valorisation des potentiels territoriaux pour un développement local inclusif dans le nord du Togo

description-proc.eng: The project "Integrated Territorial Development and Good Governance in Togo" is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). It supports the Government of Togo in advancing decentralisation and territorial development in the regions of Kara and Savanes. Despite progress in decentralisation, regional and local authorities face persistent challenges in exercising transferred competences, delivering quality public services, mobilising local revenues and promoting inclusive local economic development. These constraints are compounded by poverty, climate change, demographic pressure and a fragile security context in northern Togo. The overall objective is to enable regional and local actors to harness the social and economic potential of their territories to improve living conditions in an equitable and sustainable manner. The project applies an integrated territorial development approach with capacity development at individual, organisational and institutional levels. It cooperates with national ministries (Ministry of Local Development, Ministry of Decentralisation, Ministry of Finance), regional councils and municipalities, the National Training Agency for Local Authorities (Agence nationale de formation des collectivités territoriales, ANFCT), the National Association of Municipalities (Faîtière des Communes du Togo, FCT), civil society organisations and private sector actors. To sustain decentralisation and territorialisation efforts, the project also aims at strengthening socio-economic resilience, in particular of communities in the Northen border regions, and provide economic perspectives, in particular for young people. Activities are structured around three complementary outputs: (1) Strengthening the capacities of regional and local authorities to implement transferred competences. (2) Improving collaboration between public institutions, local authorities, civil society and the private sector for inclusive and conflict-sensitive territorial development. (3) Strengthening transparent, participatory and accountable local public financial management. Innovative elements include municipal benchmarking, peer-to-peer learning, digital solutions for local governance, performance-based management and evidence-based decision-making. Gender equality, social inclusion (LNOB), climate resilience, conflict sensitivity and digitalisation are mainstreamed across all interventions to ensure sustainable and scalable results. The assignment targets 38 municipalities in Kara and Savanes through FCT and ANFCT, with a view to progressive replication towards all 117 municipalities. Benchmarking and peer learning will be designed, piloted and institutionalised to steer capacity development and foster continuous improvement. In addition, specialised technical assistance will complement these mechanisms across the three outputs, including support for implementing transferred competences, facilitating inclusive territorial collaboration and strengthening local public financial management (e. g. participatory budgeting, revenue mobilisation, transparency and anti-corruption), while ensuring digital solutions adhere to recognised standards and are interoperable with national ecosystems.

title-proc.eng: 10022598-Short-Term Expert Pools to support negotiations and implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

description-proc.eng: Background: Although many of the world"s fastest-growing economies are in Africa, trade among African countries remains limited. The continent mostly exports raw materials and agricultural products, while it imports machinery, equipment, and food mainly from outside Africa. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which is one of the African Union"s (AU) flagship projects for the implementation of its Agenda 2063, aims to change this. It is expected that, with the introduction of the free trade zone, intra- African trade will be 15% to 25% higher by 2040 (UNECA). The AfCFTA agreement has been signed by 54 of the 55 African Union Member States (MS) and became effective under international law in May 2019. The full implementation of the AfCFTA will lead to a continental single market of more than 1.4 billion people with an aggregate GDP exceeding USD 2 trillion. Our Approach: The GIZ implemented project "Support to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) II" cofinanced by the BMZ and the EU, seeks to improve framework conditions for the realisation of the AfCFTA and supports the outstanding negotiations and the implementation of the AfCFTA. For this, the programme supports the African Union, specifically the Department for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry, Minerals (ETTIM) and the AfCFTA Secretariat at the continental level in the coordination of AfCFTA implementation. On the regional level the programme cooperates with Regional Economic Communities (RECs), specifically EAC (East African Community), ECOWAS (Economic Community for West African States) and SADC (South African Development Community, plus additional RECs based on request). The programme also supports Member States (Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, Zambia, plus additional Member States based on request) by working with national institutions, like trade ministries and customs, to implement the agreement. Lastly, the programme works closely with private sector and civil society actors to increase trade under the AfCFTA. Together with the named partners, the programme covers interventions across all technical areas of the AfCFTA. The EU co-financed part of the programme, the EU Technical Assistance Facility, operates as a multi-partner contribution agreement between the European Commission, GIZ (lead implementing agency), Expertise France, and FIAP. A Project Management Unit, which is housed in the AfCFTA Secretariat, oversees the implementation of the programme and the execution of activities.
